prompt: A socially responsible clothing store will attempt to give customers
choices: lower quality products at reduced prices.
the best products at competitive prices.
the best products no matter what the cost.
explanation: The best products at competitive prices. A socially responsible clothing store will attempt to operate in such a way as to make this possible. Producing high-quality products to sell at high prices will limit the store's market. Producing lower quality products to sell at reduced prices may harm the image of the store. Pro-ducing the best products without regard to their cost will eventually lead to financial ruin.

prompt: The manager of a local store describes the store as selling brand name or designer merchandise at lower-than-normal prices, carrying a changing collection of items that may include closeouts, samples, and irregulars. This store is considered a(n)
explanation: Off-price discounter. These stores sell brand name or designer merchandise at lower-than-normal prices. Their collections change and often include closeouts, samples, and irregulars. T.J. Maxx is an example of an off-price discounter. Discount chains, such as K mart, sell merchandise at lower than recognized market-level prices at many stores. Specialty stores, such as Claire's Accessories, carry selections of limited class-ifications of merchandise. Their prices tend to be higher than discounters but with lower volume. Factory outlets are owned and operated by the manufacturer and sell only merchandise made by the manufacturer, at reduced prices. Bass and Van Heusen are examples of factory outlets.

prompt: What is the marketing function that provides information to consumers that will assist them in making a decision to purchase a good or service?
explanation: Promotion. This function involves communicating information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome. The major elements of promotion are advertising, personal selling, publicity, and sales promotion. Pricing is determining and adjusting prices to maximize return and meet customers' perceptions of value. Production is the process or activity of producing goods or services. Distribution is moving, storing, locating, and/or transferring ownership of goods or services.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to apparel manufacturers of automating the production process?
explanation: Increased efficiency. Automation replaces human labor with machine production, thereby increasing efficien-cy and producing larger quantities of goods. A disadvantage of automation is that it increases the amount of capital that must be invested in equipment. Automating production increases computerization because most automated systems are controlled by computers. Increased consumer demand helped create the need for automation.

prompt: If a menswear store uses the accrual method of accounting, calculate the amount its records would show in sales for one month based on the following information: credit sales of $25,000, cash sales of $42,500, cash-on-hand of $3,850, and wages of $6,250.
explanation: $67,500. The accrual method of accounting records transactions at the time they occur even if no money changes hands at that time. This method is used by many menswear stores, especially those that extend credit. Since credit purchases are never paid for at the time of purchase, the accrual method keeps the store up-to-date on the amount of sales rather than on the amount of cash received. If a store made $25,000 in credit sales and $42,500 in cash sales in one month, accounting records would show $67,500 in sales for that month even though the money for the credit sales had not yet been received. Monthly sales do not include cash-on-hand or wages.

prompt: Which of the following is an important function of midlevel management?
choices: To serve as a link between toplevel and
To make sure projects meet deadlines
To establish long-term objectives for the firstline management company
explanation: To serve as a link between toplevel and firstline management. Since midlevel management operates between toplevel and firstline management, it provides the connecting link between the two. Midlevel management plans ways that the long-term objectives set by toplevel management can be reached and assigns the projects to firstline management. Making sure that projects meet deadlines and preparing workers' daily schedules are responsibilities of firstlevel management.

prompt: Which of the following is a capability of a presentation software program?
explanation: Combining animation and sound. Presentation software programs give the user the capability of presenting information by combining graphics, text, animation, photographs, and sound. Presentation software can be used to create slide programs, overhead transparencies, multimedia presentations, etc. This software enables users to develop visual presentations that are lively, colorful, and appealing to viewers. Presenta-tion software programs are not used to connect several computers, copy and print documents, or calculate mathematical data.

prompt: The use of radio frequency data communication (RFDC) allows clothing retailers to quickly perform which of the following tasks:
choices: Interact with employees on a daily basis
explanation: Verify prices of returned merchandise. The technology of radio frequency data communication (RFDC) allows clothing retailers to quickly perform a variety of tasks such as verify prices of returned merchandise. The most common application of RFDC is to attach portable scanners to a handheld data-entry device and use it to identify items by their bar-coded labels. By scanning bar codes, retailers can quickly verify prices of returned merchandise. This is often important if customers have lost their sales receipts or the item does not contain a printed price tag. The technology of RFDC does not allow retailers to print updated price labels, offer online shopping services, or interact with employees on a daily basis.

prompt: To prevent computer fraud, sportswear stores should provide employees with
choices: specialized training on the computer equipment.
an understanding of the central processing unit.
instructions not to use the computer for sensitive data.
explanation: Specialized training on the computer equipment. Specialized training could include making sure employees understand how to operate the hardware and software, how to protect their passwords from use by others, how often to copy computer files, and the proper way to report suspected computer fraud. It is unrealistic to avoid using the computer for sensitive data since most sportswear stores have a certain amount of information they consider confidential. Access to valuable data provides an opportunity for computer fraud. Operators do not need to understand the central processing unit of the computer in order to prevent fraud.

prompt: When supervising accessory store employees on the sales floor, the sales supervisor may ask them to replenish merchandise, rearrange displays, and
explanation: Clean shelves and fixtures. Helping customers and selling are the two primary responsibilities of sales-people. However, they will also have "down time," when they are not helping customers. It is important that they appear alert and engaged during these times. Sales supervisors may ask them to perform a variety of tasks, including replenishing merchandise, rearranging displays, and cleaning shelves and fixtures. There are many other tasks in a retail environment that must be accomplished, but many of these are the respon-sibility of the sales supervisor. These include, but are not limited to, preparing schedules, writing sales reports, and reviewing work performances of salespeople.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a fashion designer's intellectual property that is protected by law?
explanation: Trademarks. A trademark is a symbol, design, or word used by a producer to identify a good or service and registered with the government to prevent its use by others. A trademark is a type of intellectual property that a business owns that federal law prohibits others from using or copying without permission. An example of trademark infringement is manufacturers' making imitation goods that carry a business's trademark. Air rights, leases, and collateral are considered real property rather than intellectual property.

prompt: An occurrence that creates a communication barrier by drawing the listener's attention away from the speaker is referred to as a(n)
explanation: Distraction. A distraction interferes with transmitting and receiving messages because it diverts the listener's attention. A distortion is an intentional or unintentional change in a message. An objection is a reason a customer gives for not making a buying decision. A compromise is a solution to a conflict in which everyone agrees to a mutually acceptable solution.

prompt: A shoe store salesperson should address adult customers whose names s/he doesn't know as
explanation: Sir, Ma'am, or Miss. Sir is always appropriate for a man. Ma'am can be used for a woman wearing wedding rings or an older woman, as it is a softened version of the more formal Madame which is seldom used today. Miss is appropriate for a young woman and/or a woman without wedding rings. Avoid the use of Mrs. or Mr. unless a last name can be added to the title. You folks is an expression, not a form of address. Salespeople should never refer to a customer as buddy or honey.

prompt: Communication between clothing store employees on the same level but in different departments is known as __________ communication.
explanation: Horizontal. Communication between clothing store employees who have similar or the same positions of authority is referred to as horizontal communication. Upward communication moves from employees up to management; downward communication moves from management down to employees. Cooperative describes a positive attitude toward working with others.

prompt: When office arrangements require employees to share space, what do many sportswear store chains provide in order to offer their employees an area for privacy?
explanation: Meeting rooms with doors. Space may be tight in the headquarters of sportswear store chains and employees could be required to share offices or work in small cubicles that are noisy or in plain view of others. These types of office arrangements frequently create privacy problems because employees do not have quiet, secluded places to perform their tasks or make sensitive phone calls to customers. Many chains solve this problem by providing meeting rooms with doors that employees can use to discuss sensitive information with coworkers, talk freely with customers, or be alone to write important reports. Individual cubicles create privacy problems because they are usually close together and offer no barrier to noise. Cafeterias and recreational facilities often are crowded and noisy and do not provide private areas for employees.

prompt: Which of the following forms of transportation is very slow but inexpensive?
explanation: Water carriers. Water carriers are slow, but they provide the least expensive form of transportation, espe-cially for bulky products. Railroad transportation is relatively inexpensive but not as cheap as water. Motor carriers are more expensive than both rail and water, and air carriers are the fastest and most expensive.

prompt: Channel members' sharing inventory and order-processing information through databases and computer systems is an example of the use of technology in
explanation: Distribution. Distribution uses technology for storage, product handling, inventory control, and order process-ing. The use of new technology makes it easier for channel members to share information and track the distribution of goods. Technology in planning is often used to collect and analyze research information. Technology in pricing is often used to verify credit or debit a sale. Technology in promotion is often used to create advertising and unique displays.

prompt: If an invoice lists terms of 4/10, net 30 on a net amount of $3,675.50, calculate the total if the T-shirt shop takes the discount.
explanation: $3,528.48. Invoices list the terms that indicate when payment is expected. The terms are often expressed as discounts that are available if the T-shirt shop pays within a certain amount of time. In this example, the shop may take a 4% discount if the invoice is paid within 10 days of the invoice date. To calculate the dis-count, multiply the net amount by 4% ($3,675.50 x 4% or .04 = $147.02). Subtract this figure from the net amount to calculate the total after discount ($3,675.50 – $147.02 = $3,528.48).

prompt: An efficient order-fulfillment process can provide a competitive edge if it is based on
choices: timely and accurate information about customer orders.
explanation: Timely and accurate information about customer orders. The order processing and fulfillment processes involve the exchange of information relating to individual product orders by buyers and sellers. Therefore, in order to be successful, this process requires timely and accurate information about the orders themselves. This allows order fulfillment to occur with predictable order-cycle length and acceptable response times. By understanding customer needs, superior fulfillment systems can be designed, which provides a competitive edge. Overnight decision making is not a necessity in an efficient order-fulfillment system but may be required in certain circumstances. Technology plays a key role in order fulfillment and should be selected based on the demands of the system, not according to how expensive it is. A LIFO fulfillment process (last-in, first-out) is one way to approach fulfillment; however, there are other methods that meet different objec-tives and criteria, such as FIFO, or first-in, first-out.

prompt: Which of the following products should be moved through the receiving process the fastest?
choices: A dozen pairs of dress shoes
explanation: A dozen diamond watches. These are valuable items that need protection from theft and from being lost. They should receive priority processing, based on their value. A dozen pairs of dress shoes do not cost as much as the diamond watches, and the packages are less likely to be stolen or lost. A dozen boxes of pencils and a dozen picture frames are also not as costly or as likely to be stolen as the diamond watches.

prompt: A clothing manufacturer ships a $6,250 order by way of common carrier to a store in a city that is located 575 miles from the plant. Calculate the amount the store will pay for the order if the shipping charges are $36.75, FOB to the store.
explanation: $6,250.00. Stores usually negotiate for the most economical shipping method in order to save money on delivery charges. Common carrier, or commercial trucking company, is one of the least expensive ways to ship goods. The shipping term FOB to the store means that the manufacturer owns the goods during ship-ment and pays the charges until the order reaches the store. In this example, therefore, the store pays only the $6,250 for the order and not the $36.75 shipping charges.

prompt: An apparel manufacturer that decides to sell directly to large clothing stores rather than through wholesalers might create __________ conflict within its distribution channel.
explanation: Vertical. Conflict in a distribution channel occurs when there is disagreement among the various channel members. Vertical conflict occurs when there is disagreement between different levels of the same channel. An example of a vertical channel is an apparel manufacturer selling to wholesalers who then sell to retailers. If the manufacturer decides to bypass the wholesalers and sell directly to large clothing stores, conflict may develop within that vertical channel of distribution because the wholesalers are being eliminated. Horizontal conflict occurs among businesses at the same channel level, such as between different franchisees for the same business competing in the same city. Formal and conventional are not types of channel conflict.

prompt: Receiving clerks usually count each item in a shipment and mark it off the purchase order in order to
explanation: Identify discrepancies. One way to identify shipping discrepancies is for receiving clerks to count the items in a shipment and mark them off the purchase order. By counting each item, the receiving clerks will find out if certain items are missing or if more items were shipped than ordered. Labeling merchandise, distributing stock, and warehousing excess goods are other aspects of receiving.

prompt: What do many apparel retailers do with the merchandise that customers bring back or exchange?
explanation: Return it to stock. Apparel retailers usually accept returned merchandise from their customers. If the mer-chandise is in its original condition, retailers return the items to stock in order to resell it. Accepting returned merchandise voids the original sale; therefore, most retailers put the goods back on the selling floor as if the original sale did not occur. Retailers usually do not give returned merchandise to charities. The returned items are added to the inventory. Retailers would not send returned goods to the cleaners, but they might discount the price.

prompt: The most effective way for a bridal salon to determine the exact quantity and value of its stock is to take a(n) ___________ inventory.
explanation: Physical. A physical inventory is an actual count of the items in stock and provides the bridal salon with the exact quantities and values of stock on hand. A perpetual, or book, inventory involves continuously updating inventory records as transactions occur. Opening inventory is the amount of stock a salon has on hand at the beginning of each period.

prompt: If customers feel that a clothing item's price is too high, they will probably
explanation: Buy less of the item. Likewise, if customers feel that the price is relatively low, they will buy more. Cus-tomers affect prices of clothing items through the use of their economic votes—by deciding to buy or not to buy. Most retail prices are not negotiable or of interest to the Better Business Bureau, which tries to protect consumers from fraud. Many customers will complain about prices, but few would take the time to make a formal, written complaint.

prompt: During the month of July, sales at Handy's Shoe Mart totaled $2,500. The cost of the shoes was $1,025, and the owner paid a total of $866 for supplies, insurance, rent, and utilities during the month. Calculate the owner's net profit for the month.
explanation: $609. Net profit is the amount of money left over after operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit. Gross profit is the money left over after cost of merchandise is subtracted from sales income. To calculate net profit, first subtract cost of the shoes from total sales ($2,500 – $1,025 = $1,475). Then, subtract oper-ating expenses from that figure ($1,475 – $866 = $609).

prompt: A country's economy grows when its population grows at a slower rate than its
explanation: GDP per capita. GDP (gross domestic product) per capita is the average productivity of individual workers calculated by dividing the gross domestic product by the worker hours required to produce it. When a country's GDP per capita grows at a faster rate than its population, the country's economy can grow. The standard of living is affected by productivity. Management should improve workers' quality of work life to help to increase productivity. Capital goods are manufactured or constructed items that are used to produce goods and services.

prompt: If the Federal Reserve System increases the cost of borrowing money, what phase of the business cycle is likely to follow?
explanation: Contraction. Contraction is the phase of the business cycle characterized by decreased demand for goods and services, rising unemployment, increased saving by consumers, and reduced sales and profits for busi-nesses. Raising interest rates slow business activities, and the contraction phase often follows. Expansion is the first stage of the business cycle, characterized by increased spending and borrowing, increased demands for goods and services, increased employment rates, and decreased interest rates on loans. Peak is the second phase of the business cycle, which is the high point of economic activity and during which demand begins to exceed production capacities. Trough is the fourth phase of the business cycle, which is considered the low point of economic activity and is characterized by high rates of unemployment and busi-ness failure.

prompt: A clothing manufacturer located in a country that levies a 15% tax on imports buys a $150,000 piece of equipment from a supplier in another country. What is the cost of the equipment?
explanation: $172,500. Some nations levy taxes on imported goods in order to obtain revenue or to protect an industry that might be destroyed by foreign competition. Import taxes can be costly to businesses that buy equipment from businesses in other countries because the taxes increase the cost of the equipment. In this situation, a 15% tax is added to the cost of the equipment. To determine the final cost of the equipment, multiply the price by the percent of tax ($150,000 x 15% or .15 = $22,500). Then, add the amount of tax to the price to determine the final cost ($150,000 + $22,500 = $172,500).

prompt: Which of the following is a financing activity:
explanation: Borrowing. Borrowing is a financing activity because it involves deciding how much to borrow and making arrangements to repay the loan from anticipated profits. Licensing is the process of issuing a government permit allowing an individual or a business to function in the marketplace. Pricing is a marketing function that involves determining and adjusting prices to maximize return and meet customers' perceptions of value. Producing is the process or activity of making goods and services.

prompt: Which of the following would be the marketing information most likely to be gathered and analyzed by a marketing-information management system:
explanation: Consumer trends. A marketing-information management system can help apparel businesses to discover new or expanded markets and to use them. The system can gather and analyze information about consumer trends, target markets, changes in the environment, changing events, and the effects of these factors on consumers. A characteristic of useful marketing data is that they should be up-to-date. Historical data, therefore, would not usually be gathered. Employee absences are a management, rather than a marketing, consideration.

prompt: Software that allows for real-time analysis of marketing information enables shoe store chains to search many databases and identify
explanation: Obscure relationships. Advances in technology have created software that allows for real-time analysis of marketing information. The benefit of this software to shoe store chains is that it enables them to search many databases and identify obscure relationships. The software allows chains to analyze the data as it is collected and compare it with information stored in many other databases. For example, real-time analysis might discover that a customer applying for store credit has the same telephone number as another customer who recently declared bankruptcy. This information would be immediately made available to the credit man-ager. Pricing strategies are plans for setting prices. A hidden objection is a real objection the customer does not want brought out in the open. Distribution channels are paths, or routes, that goods or services take from the producer to the ultimate consumer or industrial user.

prompt: Which of the following is a good source of information about a menswear store's purchases:
explanation: Receiving log. The receiving record, or log, is a good source of information about a menswear store's purchases because it lists all shipments delivered to the store. The log includes specific data about each shipment such as the name of the shipper, the name of the vendor, the shipping charges, purchase order number, and date. A balance sheet indicates the store's net worth but does not detail specific purchases. Customer records indicate what customers have purchased rather than what the store has purchased. Sales records keep track of what the store has sold, not what it has purchased.

prompt: What type of internal record might provide a clothing manufacturer with marketing information about the competition and changes in the marketplace?
explanation: Sales activity reports. Individual sales representatives usually prepare monthly sales activity reports that contain information not only about sales, but also about competitors' activities and any changes that occur in the marketplace. Salespeople deal with customers daily and are in a position to find out what their competi-tors are doing in order to sell their products. This might include information about sales techniques, specialpricing, unique services, or credit arrangements. Salespeople also find out when customers' preferences change and when they may have more money available to spend. Clothing manufacturers review this type of marketing information in order to remain competitive and meet customers' changing needs. Accounts receivable reports indicate all the monies owed to a manufacturer by its customers. Customer comment cards provide information about how customers rate the manufacturer's overall performance. Employee performance reviews evaluate performance on the job.

prompt: Sportswear store chains often obtain marketing information that identifies potential threats from competitors during the process of conducting
explanation: Environmental scans. Environmental scanning is the process of tracking external changes that affect a sports-wear store chain and its market. Chains often conduct scans of external environments, such as social, economic, political, and competitive, in order to identify changes or threats that may have an impact on their operations. During this process, chains might identify potential threats from competitors, such as new goods and services, additional locations, lower prices, or aggressive advertising. The marketing information obtained from environmental scans will help chains to deal with potential threats and make necessary changes in order to remain competitive. Operational reviews evaluate a chain's internal operations. Developmental tests are intended to evaluate new goods and services. Governmental surveys are conducted by government agencies.

prompt: After collecting various types of marketing information, lingerie stores often use databases to __________ the data.
explanation: Organize. Using databases to organize data is one way that lingerie stores transform data into useful mar-keting information. The use of databases allows stores to organize data, such as the basic characteristics of customers, into a format that is easy to read and understand. Once the data is organized, it becomes marketing information that stores can analyze and review in order to make effective marketing decisions. Validating marketing information involves determining whether the information is accurate. Databases are not able to describe or forecast marketing information. They are only able to organize the data according to certain characteristics.

prompt: Based on the sales volume information contained in the following database, which salesperson sold the least amount of designer purses: Salesperson Purse 1 Purse 2 Purse 3 Salesperson A 2,450 3,270 1,900 Salesperson B 1,720 3,660 2,350 Salesperson C 2,280 3,140 2,190 Salesperson D 1,960 3,850 1,920
explanation: Salesperson C. Purse manufacturers usually maintain a variety of sales information in databases, but this information is not valuable unless the manufacturers analyze it. For example, a manufacturer might keep track of the amount of purses that each salesperson sells. Then, a manufacturer might analyze that data to determine which salesperson sold the least and which salesperson sold the most. The salesperson who sold the least might need additional training or other type of assistance from the manufacturer to increase the level of sales. In this situation, Salesperson C sold the least amount of purses (2,280 + 3,140 + 2,190 = 7,610). Salesperson A sold 7,620 purses and both Salesperson B and D sold 7,730 purses.

prompt: One of the main portions of a marketing report describes the research methods and the
explanation: Data collection procedures. One portion of a marketing report contains a detailed explanation and descrip-tion of the research methods and how the data were collected. This section should explain what types of secondary data were used and how the primary data were collected (questionnaire, telephone survey, etc.). This section also should provide a description of the questions that were asked and a profile of the people who were surveyed. A detailed description of research methods and data collection procedures adds cred-ibility to the report. Marketing reports do not describe industry review standards or consulting expenses. Technical terminology is explained throughout the report rather than in one specific section.

prompt: An apparel marketer who changes the product element in the marketing mix should re-evaluate the other marketing elements because the elements are
explanation: Interrelated. If apparel marketers change one element of the marketing mix, they should carefully examine the other elements because the others will probably also need to be changed. The marketing mix elements depend on each other, rather than being independent or detached. The elements are not unique—the same elements can be used by other companies.

prompt: Calculate a uniform store's sales forecast for next year based on the following information: 90% of the 500 current customers say they will buy again next year and spend an average of $750. Thirty of the competitor's customers say they will buy and spend an average of $500.
explanation: $352,500. Uniform stores often use several forecasting techniques to estimate sales for the coming year because various factors affect the forecast. Some of these factors include the number of existing customers who will continue to buy and the number of a competitor's customers who will buy for the first time. Stores may gather forecasting information from customer surveys and from salespeople who may have contact with the competitor's customers. In this example, 90% of the 500 current customers will continue to buy and spend an average of $750. Calculate that amount by multiplying the number of customers by the percent (500 x 90% or .90 = 450). The 450 current customers will each spend $750 for a total of $337,500 ($750 x 450 = $337,500). Thirty of the competitor's customers will spend $500 each for a total of $15,000 ($500 x 30 = $15,000). Add the two amounts to calculate next year's sales forecast ($337,500 + $15,000 = $352,500).

prompt: One of the reasons that teams are important to accessory manufacturers is that they can increase
explanation: Productivity. Productivity is the amount and value of goods and services produced (outputs) from set amounts of resources (inputs). The overall output of all employees is often increased when accessory manufacturers use teams because workers who feel they are an important part of a team often work harder and produce more. Other reasons that teams are important to manufacturers are that they reduce costs and workplace conflicts. Teams do not increase procrastination—putting off until tomorrow what should have been done today.

prompt: What should you do to demonstrate a customer-service mindset in the following situation: An irate dress shop customer yells at you because of a billing error.
choices: Get as upset as the customer.
Make sure the mistake is corrected.
Call the person's supervisor to complain about the customer's attitude.
explanation: Make sure the mistake is corrected. The customer wants you to resolve the problem. To do this, you must find solutions and correct the mistake without getting as upset as the customer, being defensive, or placing blame. You must find out what happened so that you know what to do next. Calling the customer's super-visor is inappropriate. You should look at this problem as an opportunity to discover how you can improve your customer-service skills.

prompt: The ability to empathize with customers is tied very closely to the shoe salesperson's ability to
explanation: Listen. Listening is one of the guidelines that shoe salespeople should follow in order to improve their ability to empathize. Salespeople should listen attentively to customers to find out what they have to say. By listening, salespeople will be able to understand customers. Once they understand customers, salespeople will be able to empathize with them. Speaking, writing, and describing are not guidelines that salespeople should follow in order to improve their ability to empathize.

prompt: A specialty boutique employee should attempt to help difficult customers because while helping them, the employee can
explanation: Try to build a clientele. Difficult customers are often hard to please, but when these customers are satisfied with the products purchased and the treatment received, they often become repeat customers. Helping difficult customers may not prevent a confrontation or make them happy. Displaying product knowledge is not an acceptable reason for helping customers.

prompt: Calculate a discount clothing store's fixed costs based on the following information: $55,000 in rent, $250,250 in salaries, $6,750 for insurance, $72,400 in commissions, and $3,700 in advertising.
explanation: $315,700. A fixed cost is the sum of all the costs incurred by a discount clothing store that usually remain at the same level no matter how many units of a product are produced or marketed. Fixed costs include rent, salaries, insurance, and the cost of an advertising campaign. Commissions are a type of variable cost because they increase or decrease in proportion to sales volume. In this example, add the cost of rent, salaries, insurance, and advertising to determine fixed costs ($55,000 + $250,250 + $6,750 + $3,700 = $315,700).

prompt: A prominent characteristic of responsible employees is that they
choices: do what they say they will do.
are only motivated by wage increases.
explanation: Do what they say they will do. You can depend upon people who are responsible because they do what they say they will do. They do not work only for pay raises, make promises whether they can fulfill them or not, or try to make their work fill the maximum amount of time.

prompt: What activity are Nikki and Josh performing when they read over a scenario and then act out the parts in a training class?
explanation: Role-playing. Role-playing is the process of assuming roles and acting through a given situation. Josh and Nikki read a scenario and role-played the parts. Brainstorming is a creative thinking technique that involves the identification of as many different ideas as possible during a certain time frame. Experimenting is the act of testing or trying out a proposed idea or procedure. Meditation, which is a mental exercise, is the act of contemplating, reflecting, or thinking over.

prompt: Jane has just congratulated herself for getting an A on a test. What kind of feedback is this?
explanation: Internal. The judgments that you make about yourself are referred to as internal feedback because their source is within you. It is not unusual because, whether you are fully conscious of it or not, you are involved in a process of selfevaluation almost all of the time. External feedback comes from sources outside your-self. Internal feedback is direct rather than indirect.

prompt: A goal is an objective that a person plans to
explanation: Achieve. Goals are objectives that people plan to achieve. They are definite ideas about something that people want in order to satisfy a particular need. Most people's goals are based on their wants and needs. In order to achieve their goals, people first identify, define, and establish them.

prompt: Which of the following often is a good source of career information in the local community:
explanation: Trade associations. A trade association is a group of persons in the same industry or geographic area who form a society to solve their common problems. Local trade associations often are an excellent source of career information because they know what types of jobs are available in their industry in the community. For example, the local builders' association knows which construction companies are hiring and for which jobs. Regional magazines usually do not contain career information. National corporations are a source of local career information only if they have locations in the community. Library publications usually do not focus on career information.

prompt: A job application usually requests information about employment history and may ask the applicant to explain why s/he
explanation: Left a previous job. Applications often ask the applicants why they left previous jobs. Acceptable answers include leaving to take better jobs, leaving because the jobs were seasonal, and leaving to continue educa-tion. Applicants should avoid making negative comments about former employers. Businesses want to know if applicants left previous jobs for good reasons or if they have a habit of changing jobs frequently for no reason. The job application does not ask why the applicant attended certain schools, volunteered com-munity service, or did military duty.

prompt: What type of information can be included in an interview followup letter?
explanation: Brief reminder of qualifications. It is acceptable for applicants to include a brief reminder of their qualifica-tions in an interview followup letter. Restating that they are qualified for the position is one way of saying that they are interested and would like to have the job. The reminder of qualifications should be very brief because the applicants will have covered that topic in detail during the interview. Information about employ-ment history, education, and salary expectations is discussed in the interview and should not be reviewed in a followup letter.

prompt: Apparel store employees who want to enhance their careers and progress through the management ranks should develop their
explanation: Leadership skills. Leadership is the ability to guide or direct the actions of others in a desired manner. Apparel store employees who want to progress through the ranks of management should develop their leadership skills because they will be expected to supervise and lead their subordinates. Employees who demonstrate good leadership skills often are given more responsibility and authority over others. Employees who want to enhance their careers often develop their professional contacts rather than their social contacts. Job expectations are what employees hope to accomplish or achieve in their careers. Employees do not need to develop their artistic abilities in order to progress through the management ranks.

prompt: The individual who coordinates the clothing merchandise of several retail departments is a
explanation: Merchandise manager. A merchandise manager coordinates the clothing merchandise of several retail departments and oversees classification buyers. A department manager runs a department according to the framework of a company's overall plan and is responsible for the arrangement of goods on the selling floor, merchandise counts, and the supervision of salespeople within the department. A store manager is the top person in charge of every aspect of a store's operations. A successful store manager would be promoted to the position of district manager to oversee multiple stores.

prompt: Which of the following technologies allow T-shirt shops to quickly determine the effect that different prices will have on the bottom line before setting the prices of various items:
explanation: Computer software. Various types of computer software programs enable T-shirt shops to experiment with prices before deciding on the actual price to charge. A shop can plug in different prices for various items to find out what effect each price will have on the bottom line. Shops use computer software programs to determine which price will be the most profitable as well as the most appealing to customers before setting the price. Shops do not use digital imaging, point-of-sale systems, or optical scanning to experiment with different prices.

prompt: The selling prices of outerwear help buyers to
explanation: Make buying decisions. Most buyers feel price indicates quality, and they use selling price as a guide in selecting outerwear to buy. Selling price is helpful in comparing the value of similar, rather than different, coats. Selling price does not provide buyers with enough information to allow them to determine how much markup is included in an item's price. Whether a buyer spends freely is determined by the amount of money s/he has to spend.

prompt: What helps product planners predict whether a new style of watch will be successful before a manufacturer makes a major investment?
explanation: Marketing information. Market research is often used to aid product planners in gathering information con-cerning consumer needs and preferences. Marketers must be knowledgeable about the market and about consumers' buying habits in order to offer watches that will be purchased. Market information helps planners to predict whether a new watch will be successful before the manufacturer makes a major investment. Prod-uct monitoring, on the other hand, takes place after a watch is established in the market and after monies have been invested in a watch. A company's goals influence the choice of watches to offer and suggest ways for the business to grow and remain competitive either by developing entirely new watches or develop-ing watches similar to those being introduced by the competition. After products are introduced on the mar-ket, they move through life cycles: the courses that products follow in the market including their introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.

prompt: A new fashion simultaneously appears in high-priced boutiques, moderately priced department stores, and discounters. This is an example of the __________ theory of fashion origin.
explanation: Trickle across. The trickle across theory says fashion is simultaneously adopted by groups at all socioeco-nomic levels. Therefore, high, moderate, and low-priced versions appear in different stores at about the same time. Trickle down indicates that fashions begin with exclusive stores and move down to lower priced stores. Trickle up indicates that fashions begin with lower priced, work-type clothing and move up to be popular with everyone. Cycles across is not a fashion theory.

prompt: What element contributes the greatest visual impact without affecting the price of apparel?
explanation: Color. The choice of specific design details, fabric choice, and trim can considerably increase a garment's cost, but the color changes the appearance without adding expense.

prompt: To reduce lag time between order and delivery and to adjust sizes, colors, and patterns of its apparel collections in response to actual sales, a major retail chain uses __________ with its foreign manufacturers.
explanation: Electronic data interchange. EDI provides a nearly instantaneous system for the transfer of information. This linking system allows business to scan the sale of an item at a pointofsale terminal and send the resulting information directly to the vendor to be used to plan production and delivery in order to precisely match customer shopping. EDI replaces buyer's intuition with more precise and faster product management. Distribution centers are shipping centers for merchandise en route to the sales floor.

prompt: Any business that transports apparel items across state lines must comply with standards set by
explanation: Government agencies. Government agencies develop standards that usually apply to goods and services that the government regulates. The U.S. Department of Commerce establishes standards for such activities as interstate commerce and transportation. Any business that transports apparel items across state lines must comply with these government standards. Not all businesses will set interstate transportation stan-dards. Trade associations and professional organizations often establish standards for their members; however, not all businesses belong to these groups.

prompt: Two major cities that influence trends and fashion in the apparel and accessory industry are
choices: New York City, U.S.A. and Frankfort, Germany.
explanation: Tokyo, Japan and London, England. Many large cities are considered hubs or centers for the fashion industry. In addition to Tokyo and London, New York City, Paris, and Milan are cities in which many designers live and work and set the tone for fashion and style. Frankfort, Belfast, and Liverpool are not generally considered fashion centers.

prompt: A specialty boutique whose target market is the career woman with expensive taste would have a product mix with __________ assortment.
explanation: Narrow variety, deep. The terms used to describe the scope of a boutique's product mix include broad or narrow and shallow or deep. A product mix with narrow variety refers to a limited number of product lines. A deep assortment refers to a great many items in each product line. This boutique offers a great many items of clothing and accessories but only in a few product lines. A broad product mix offers many product lines. A shallow mix offers few items in the product line.

prompt: A brand name should be distinctive so that it
choices: gives the shoes a generic image.
can be used in multinational marketing.
can easily be changed over time.
sets the shoes apart from other shoes.
explanation: Sets the shoes apart from other shoes. The brand name should not be too common or too similar to those used by competitors. It should be appropriate and even clever, if possible. A brand name's adaptability makes it useable in multinational marketing and prevents it from needing to be changed over time. A dis-tinctive brand name gives the shoes a specific image, not a generic image.

prompt: Open-to-buy is a versatile tool that a busy bridal salon can use to control purchasing activities on a(n) __________ basis.
explanation: Daily, weekly, or monthly. A busy bridal salon will use the open-to-buy method to make purchasing decisions on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis. Although open-to-buy budgets might be set up on a quarterly or annual basis, purchasing decisions are normally ongoing in most retail stores. Open-to-buy is not a long-range planning tool.

prompt: Which of the following is not a category of planned reductions on a merchandise plan:
explanation: Cash discounts. A cash discount is a reduction in price given to a buyer who pays an invoice within a specified number of days according to the terms of the invoice. Markdowns, merchandise shortages, and employee discounts represent reductions that are planned for during the season because they help to determine the amount of money available for purchasing.

prompt: In order to communicate with the consumers who are most likely to buy their products, clothing marketers first need to
explanation: Identify their target audience. Communication must be appropriate to the receiver in order for it to be effec-tive. This means that clothing marketers must identify their target audience, or target market, and plan their communications for that audience. Studying their own industry might be part of identifying the target audi-ence. Evaluating past ads and choosing media are other steps in the promotional communication process.

prompt: The effectiveness of corporate, or institutional, promotion is often difficult to measure because
choices: it is difficult to measure people's feelings.
intangible services cannot be effectively promoted.
large numbers of people are employed in corporations.
consumers don't see all of a company's advertisements.
explanation: It is difficult to measure people's feelings. This is true in most cases. Statisticians can only measure, on a long-term basis, increased sales. An intangible service can be promoted just as effectively as a tangible product. The number of people employed in corporations has little to do with measuring the promotion's success. The fact that consumers don't see all of a company's advertisements also would not affect measur-ing their success.

prompt: The main purpose of the copy in a print ad is to
choices: show the accessory product in use.
create desire for the accessory product.
compare the accessory product to similar products.
explanation: Create desire for the accessory product. Advertising copywriters try to select an approach to the accessory product that will make readers of the ad want to purchase the product. In some cases, the copy does com-pare the product to other, similar products, but that is a method of creating desire. Illustrations show the product in use, and an ad's headline should attract the reader's attention.

prompt: When is the use of email an effective direct-advertising strategy?
choices: The message is too short for surface mailing.
A clothing store wants to be sure people read the message.
The message appeals only to people who have computers.
The message appeals to a small audience interested in a specific product.
explanation: The message appeals to a small audience interested in a specific product. The use of email allows a cloth-ing store to target small audiences spread over a vast geographic area. Email, however, can be ignored as easily as other advertising messages. Most email advertising does not deal specifically with computer related products. Message length is irrelevant.

prompt: So Internet users can move easily through a clothing store's web site and know where they are at all times within the web site, the web designer must carefully plan the
explanation: Navigation system. The navigation system refers to the method in which an Internet user moves through a clothing store's web-site pages to get from one location to another. The web-site designer should make it easy for users to know where they are at all times and be able to move to another page or site quickly and efficiently to lower the risk of frustration. The domain name is the business's web address. Although it is an important consideration in the overall web-site development process, it does not necessarily affect how well the users maneuver through the web site. The web-site reach refers to the percentage of the web users that visit a site during a set time period compared to all web users. Although management can estimate its reach, the web designers cannot control how many users visit a web site at any given time. Interaction refers to the flow of information between two sources. Interaction rate is not a term that is widely used in the e-commerce industry in relation to promotional efforts.

prompt: Should a sportswear store that buys advertising from the media expect the media to present its news releases as a favor to a customer?
choices: Yes, the advertising contract also covers news releases.
No, the store should ask the media to provide publicity.
Yes, an advertiser should expect the media to use its releases.
No, there is no connection between news releases and advertising.
explanation: No, there is no connection between news releases and advertising. Sportswear stores should not use the terms "publicity" or "advertising" in any conversations with an editor because these two functions are com-pletely separate. The store's job is to provide the media with news they can present, not to try to get them to give the store publicity.

prompt: Which of the following is a promotional activity that menswear stores should coordinate with their special promotions:
explanation: Visual merchandising. Menswear stores should coordinate the various promotional activities such as visual merchandising, signage, and advertising when conducting special promotions. The purpose of the promotion is to attract customers, and coordinating all the promotional activities creates a stronger focus. For example, the displays in the store should promote the same theme as the advertising and the special events. Product planning, information gathering, and sales training are not promotional activities.

prompt: An upscale clothing store features a line of expensive shoes in a shadowbox display window. This is an example of a(n) __________ window.
explanation: Enclosed. A shadowbox window is a variation of an enclosed window that is small and boxlike. A semi-enclosed window has a partial background that blocks out part of the store's interior from the window. An open window has no background panel and allows passersby to see inside the store. An island window is a four-sided display window often found in lobbies.

prompt: Which of the following is an important part of display maintenance:
choices: Choosing an effective principle of design
explanation: Replacing missing items immediately. Display items may be removed from the display because they have become soiled, been damaged or stolen, or sold. Many clothing stores do not sell items directly from a display because it will disrupt the display and damage its appearance. However, even these stores will occasionally agree to sell a displayed item when no other item is available for the customer to purchase. When this happens, an appropriate replacement item should be put in the display as quickly as possible. The alternatives are actions taken in creating a display.

prompt: Determine whether the following statement is true or false: When planning a display, the first step is to select a theme for the display.
choices: False, the theme is not important in planning displays.
True, the theme is more important than the merchandise.
True, merchandise should be chosen to support the theme.
False, merchandise to be displayed should be chosen first.
explanation: False, merchandise to be displayed should be chosen first. The first step in planning a display is to select the most appropriate merchandise for promotion. The items chosen for promotion may suggest a theme or lend themselves to a particular theme. The theme should help to promote the merchandise, not vice versa.

prompt: Which of the following is a tangible product:
explanation: Diamond ring. Tangible items can be perceived through the senses. Dry cleaning, lawn care, and a haircut are services, which are intangible products.

prompt: One way that salespeople for apparel manufacturers can provide quality service and develop successful relationships with business customers is by
choices: working with key people in the organization.
explanation: Working with key people in the organization. Salespeople for apparel manufacturers need to understand the needs and problems of key people in the retail organization in order to provide quality service. Salespeople will be able to gain information about how the business operates by contacting and working with these people. When salespeople are knowledgeable about a business's needs, they are able to satisfy those needs and provide quality service. The result usually is a successful relationship that benefits both the salesperson and the business customer. Salespeople should not make unannounced sales visits, criticize competitors' products, or make idle conversation during sales calls.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to clothing store supply salespeople of building a clientele:
explanation: Referrals to new prospects. Loyal customers often provide clothing store supply salespeople with leads for locating and gaining access to new prospects who may become clients. These leads may involve introduc-tions or letters of referral. Building a clientele usually increases the salesperson's paperwork load, which is not considered a benefit. The use of effective follow-up techniques helps to build a clientele, rather than being a benefit of building a clientele. Building a clientele does not increase lead time, the amount of time between placing an order and receiving the stock.

prompt: Manufacturers often provide special instructions on apparel labels that salespeople can use to
choices: show customers how to return apparel.
explanation: Explain care techniques to customers. Label information often includes care and maintenance instructions for the apparel item in an attempt to ensure its satisfactory use. The salesperson should be familiar with the information provided on the labels of the apparel items s/he sells in order to explain care techniques to customers during the selling process. Labels are not intended to facilitate returns or be used for developing visual merchandising displays. Salespeople do not promote apparel to competitors.

prompt: Levi and Jantzen are examples of __________ brands.
explanation: National. National brands are well-known brands of merchandise available in many stores in different parts of the country or the world. They represent brand names of the manufacturers. Private brands are goods made by or for a particular store or distributor. Store brands are brands that carry the name of the store that sells them. Signature brands carry the name of a well-known personality.

prompt: When evaluating the fit of a man's suit, a salesperson should make sure that the
choices: seam of the sleeve falls below the shoulder joint.
hem of the pants falls one inch above the top of the shoe.
explanation: Jacket covers the buttocks. If the jacket does not cover the buttocks, the salesperson should suggest another size, because the jacket does not fit properly. The hem of the pants should touch the top of the shoe. The lapels should lie flat and never pucker. Finally, the seam of the sleeve should be at the shoulder joint.

prompt: The part of an apparel item's brand that is most useful in a selling situation is the brand
explanation: Name. The brand name is the part of a brand that can be spoken, such as a word, phrase, letter, number, or any combination of these. Salespersons can refer to apparel items by their brand names during the selling process. A brand's position is the way consumers see the brand as compared with competitive brands. Brand strategy is an action a business takes with a brand in order to accomplish its goals. Brand extension is the brand strategy of using successful brand names to introduce new products.

prompt: A customer has returned to a coat rack for the second time and is examining the label and material of a particular coat. Which of the following types of approaches should be used:
explanation: Merchandise. A merchandise approach is a comment or question that helps direct the customer's attention to the merchandise. It usually refers to the goods on display in which the customer seems to be showing an interest. If a customer takes a second look at merchandise and examines labels and material, the sales-person should use an approach that takes advantage of the customer's interest in the product. The greeting approach would not serve this purpose since it is intended to make the customer feel welcome. The service approach is an offer of general assistance.

prompt: What style of clothing would a salesperson probably show to a customer who is dressed in a pleated skirt, white blouse, and navy blazer?
explanation: Classic. By analyzing what a customer is wearing, a salesperson can select clothing items that probably would appeal to that customer. For example, a customer who is wearing a pleated skirt, white blouse, and navy blazer is wearing a classic style of clothing. Classic clothing is traditional, conservative clothing that remains in style year after year, such as navy blazers. The customer wearing classic clothing is most likely interested in that style rather than romantic, dramatic, or faddish, because these styles quickly lose their popularity.

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that often affects organizational buying behavior:
explanation: Multiple decision makers. In many large clothing chains, there are several people who are responsible for making buying decisions. These people often have different opinions about what the company should buy or from whom they should buy. Frequently, a few people are responsible for gathering information and then a group meets to discuss the choices. The group must reach a consensus which may mean that it takes a long time for the final buying decision to be made. Day-to-day activities, local reference groups, and social class structures do not affect organizational buying behavior.

prompt: In order to determine children's correct body measurements, the salesperson should know how to use and read a
explanation: Tape measure. This is a flexible cloth or plastic measuring tape, usually from 36 to 60 inches in length, that can be wrapped around the child's waist, chest, and hips in order to obtain accurate measurements. A ruler is 12 inches in length and is not suitable for measuring curved surfaces. A calculator is used to do math-ematical computations, not in measuring. A Brannock device is used to measure shoe size.

prompt: The customer asked the salesperson for a casual blouse. The salesperson suggested a blouse with short sleeves and a club collar or a shell with a scoop neck. What was the salesperson describing?
explanation: Style characteristics of blouses. Style characteristics, or styling details, are the distinctive features of a garment that help to identify it or set it apart from another garment. Women's blouses are available with a variety of style characteristics including collars, necklines, and sleeves. Coordinating outfits involves selecting garments that complement each other when worn together. Fashion trends are the directions in which clothing styles are moving. Price range was not mentioned.

prompt: When a sportswear salesperson uses product substitution skillfully, all of the following are results that benefit the store except
explanation: Lower personnel turnover. While a reduced personnel turnover rate could benefit a sportswear store, it is not the result of product substitution. Stores benefit when salespeople are skillful in the use of product substi-tution because customers' needs are met and they are likely to become repeat customers, sales are higher since fewer sales are lost, and the store gains a good reputation.

prompt: What is a physical characteristic or quality of a raincoat?
explanation: Feature. A feature is a physical characteristic or quality of a product that explains what it is. It is something that the customer can touch, feel, smell, see, or measure. Satisfaction is a benefit customers receive from a product. A benefit refers to the advantage of the product to the customer. A buying motive is a reason customers buy.

prompt: When the customer says, "I'm just getting ideas," the shoe salesperson should recognize the statement as a
explanation: Buying excuse. When customers have made no specific buying decisions or don't want to listen to a sales presentation, they often make such responses to the shoe salesperson's offer of assistance. Additional conversation may interest the customer in a product and lead to a sale. Customers should not be ignored or pressured. A product objection is a customer's reason for not buying a particular product.

prompt: What do jewelry salespeople need to consider when selling goods or services to an individual?
explanation: Personality. Personality is a person's distinctive traits, qualities, or behavior. People have different person-alities; therefore, jewelry salespeople need to consider the personality of each customer and tailor their selling methods to appeal to that person. Some people need a lot of information, some are decisive, and others are energetic. Considering the unique personality of each customer will help salespeople to be successful. A person's environment and education might provide clues to her/his personality. Adaptability is the ability to adjust to change, which is a characteristic that may be difficult for a salesperson to identify.

prompt: Why do successful textile salespeople follow up after the sales presentation?
choices: To increase the size of the sale
To develop a professional sales presentation
explanation: To ensure customer satisfaction. A sale does not end when an order is signed or payment is received. Good selling requires followup to ascertain customer satisfaction. The size of the sale would not be increased because followup occurs after the sale; however, follow-up may lead to future sales. Exercising good sales techniques and developing a sales presentation are always secondary to customer satisfaction and service.

prompt: A customer purchased a sale item with an original selling price of $14.95. At the time of the sale, the item was reduced 20% and sales tax was 5%. How much did the customer pay for the item?
explanation: $12.56. Multiply the selling price by the percent of markdown to determine the price reduction ($14.95 x 20% or .20 = $2.99). Subtract this amount from the selling price to determine the sale price ($14.95 – $2.99 = $11.96). Multiply the sale price by the tax rate to determine tax and add to find total price ($11.96 x 5% or .05 = $.598 or $.60; $11.96 + $.60 = $12.56).

prompt: A new customer presents a temporary check drawn on his/her new checking account at a local bank. The check has been encoded by the bank and is made out correctly. Should the accessory store accept this check?
choices: Yes, the account is at a local bank.
No, temporary checks are not negotiable.
No, the customer is not known to the store.
explanation: Yes, temporary checks are acceptable. When a bank customer opens a checking account, the bank usually provides several temporary checks encoded with the customer's account number for the customer to use until his/her own checks have been printed. These checks are equivalent to a regular check, although some stores will not accept them because they indicate a new account. The store should follow its own standard procedure in identifying the customer and accepting the check.

prompt: Putting a customer's purchases in a store bag and stapling the receipt to the outside of the bag is one way of increasing the clothing store's
explanation: Security. Bagging and wrapping customers' purchases is one way that clothing stores increase their secur-ity. Salespeople and cashiers often insist on bagging or wrapping customer purchases before customers leave the store. In some cases, the bag must be stapled shut with the receipt. The wrapping identifies the customer as having paid for the goods. This is a security measure that enables store personnel to detect shoplifters who are trying to leave the store carrying unwrapped items. Bagging customers' purchases often helps to decrease expenses by reducing the amount of goods lost to shoplifters. Bagging does not increase a store's quality. Bagging and wrapping materials are supplies that most stores routinely keep on hand as a convenience to customers.

prompt: Which of the following functions is performed automatically by most electronic cash registers:
explanation: Listing purchases. Electronic cash registers automatically perform a number of functions that include listing the customer's purchases, computing tax, and calculating change due. These cash registers do not auto-matically correct errors. The correction must be made by the cash register operator. The registers calculate the amount of change due but do not dispense it to the customer. The information recorded by the cash register helps the business to calculate stockturn, which is the number of times stock is sold and replaced within a given time period.

prompt: Often, salespeople for apparel manufacturers who are prospecting can obtain lists of current and past customers, credit records, and inquiries from
explanation: Their own companies. Salespeople should make use of information available from within their own apparel manufacturing companies before looking outside. Noncompeting salespeople and trade associations usually do not have access to information about your current or past customers, their credit records, or their product inquiries. The Wall Street Journal is a business trade paper that contains such information as stock prices, advertising, science, money matters, and national and international business news.

prompt: Which of the following describes a good sales quota:
choices: It is set at a high level but is attainable.
It is set at the same level for all sales staff.
It is stated in terms that are clear to management.
It is low so that it can be reached by all sales staff.
explanation: It is set at a high level but is attainable. Good sales quotas should motivate clothing salespeople to exert their best efforts. This happens when quotas are high, rather than being set so that they are too easy to reach. At the same time, quotas should not be set so high that salespeople know they cannot possibly reach the desired goal. Therefore, sales quotas need to be realistically attainable. Quotas should be simply stated so that all personnel understand what is being asked of them. To be fair, sales quotas should be based on an individual salesperson's ability and territory. Therefore, sales quotas should not be set at the same level but at the same level of difficulty.
